stories.headline: Premier Cho Jung-tai's Japan World Baseball Classic trip sparks political controversy
stories.summary: Premier Cho Jung-tai attended a World Baseball Classic game in Tokyo, paying for the trip personally. The visit was hailed as 'baseball diplomacy' by supporters but drew criticism from opposition parties. This marked the first such visit by a Taiwan premier since 1972.

stories.headline: President Lai announces 1.25 trillion NT defense budget and AI military modernization
stories.summary: President Lai Ching-te announced an eight-year special defense budget of 1.25 trillion New Taiwan dollars and declared Taiwan will never surrender to the CCP. The announcement was made at a conference marking the 30th anniversary of Taiwan's first direct presidential election.

stories.headline: Beijing criticizes President Lai over Japanese colonial rule comments
stories.summary: Beijing accused President Lai Ching-te of 'glorifying Japanese colonial rule' after he said early KMT rule over Taiwan was 'worse than the colonial regime.' Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson called the remarks a distortion of history and an attempt to ingratiate with Japan.

Lai emphasized Taiwan's role in supply chain resilience and called for closer cooperation among democratic partners.

stories.headline: KMT and TPP approve cooperation agreement for local elections
stories.summary: Taiwan's main opposition Kuomintang and the Taiwan People's Party approved a cooperation agreement for local elections later this year. The two parties agreed to jointly field candidates in certain constituencies.

articles.title: KMT, TPP approve cooperation pact for local elections

stories.headline: Premier Cho advances domestic policy initiatives on migrant workers and UAV industry
stories.summary: Premier Cho Jung-tai approved expansion of eligibility to hire migrant domestic helpers and announced plans to develop Taiwan's UAV industry over five years with NT$44.2 billion in funding.

articles.title: Premier greenlights migrant domestic helper eligibility expansion
